scope: Three inventories: (1) .claude/hooks five-hook audit with deliberate negative tests, (2) .cursor/ config tracking status, (3) AGENT_CONTRACT.md currency vs observed lane behavior in _inbox/ close artifacts.

hooks.purpose: M1 repo-posture gate (blocks dispatches into no-touch/retiring repos), M3 CANON-PREAMBLE freshness, M4 AGENT-CONTRACT hash currency, M5 PLAN-ROW existence in OPS-16.
hooks.evidence: M4 stale-contract BLOCKED exit 2; M5 missing PLAN-ROW BLOCKED exit 2; M5 bogus P-9999 BLOCKED exit 2; M3 stale preamble vaaaaaaaa BLOCKED exit 2 with current v0f465c77 pasted; M1 no-touch smartcity-os BLOCKED exit 2 via 'repo:' line. Clean compliant input PASSED exit 0. Live proof of production firing: _catalog/canon_overrides.log carries 13 CANON_OVERRIDE entries 2026-08-13..2026-08-14.
hooks.finding: TWO fail-open defects, both silently-dead-control class. (A) canon-gate.ps1:258 extracts only /P-\d+/ from the PLAN-ROW line, so any non-P row id skips validation entirely via the 'if (-not $rowIds) { return ok }' fallthrough at :259. PROVEN: PLAN-ROW G-9999, Q-42, and the literal string 'not-a-row-at-all' ALL passed exit 0. This program (OPS-17, 37 G-rows including this dispatch's own G-05) is therefore entirely UNGATED at M5. (B) canon-gate.ps1:85-98 Resolve-RepoFromText requires a 'repo:' line, a 'git -C'/'Working in'/'worktree:' prefix, a QUOTED path, or a gh org slug. A bare unquoted 'P:/smartcity-os' in prose resolves to null and the M1 no-touch gate passes open. PROVEN: bare-path variant exit 0, all five other phrasings exit 2. Bare path is the most natural way to name a repo in a hand-written brief.

hooks.purpose: OPS-14 precondition 1b. Rejects executor briefs missing any of four ruled clauses: CANON-PREAMBLE marker, no-nesting clause as FIRST line, exit-bounded verification, machine-checkable close artifact.
hooks.evidence: Deliberate negative test blocked with exit 2 reporting all four clauses missing (raw output in negativeTest below). Clean input with all four clauses passed exit 0. Live proof: _catalog/dispatch_overrides.log carries 21 DISPATCH_OVERRIDE entries 2026-08-09..2026-08-14.
hooks.finding: Fail-open paths are deliberate and documented (:22). Real weakness is CLAUSE-DETECTION BY SUBSTRING: patterns at :143, :153, :159 match bare phrases anywhere in the text. Measured accidentally during testing - a brief whose prose merely DESCRIBES the missing clauses ('no exit-bounded verification language', 'no named close artifact path') satisfied checks 3 and 4 and reduced a four-clause failure to a one-clause failure. Any brief that mentions the word 'timeout' (in the :153 alternation) satisfies check 3 without carrying an exit-bounded rule. Also :114 exempts every brief under 400 chars from all four checks.

hooks.purpose: OPS-14 precondition 1a. Blocks git push from doc_repo when _STATE.md or MEMORY.md carry uncommitted WORKTREE edits that the push would strand.
hooks.evidence: Negative test: appended a scratch marker to _STATE.md, fed a 'git push origin main' payload, hook BLOCKED exit 2 naming _STATE.md. CLOSE_OVERRIDE=1 variant passed exit 0 and logged. _STATE.md reverted via git checkout, verified clean.
hooks.finding: Coverage hole at :90-99. When the command carries no explicit cd, the gate falls back to the SHELL cwd and exits open if that cwd is not doc_repo. PROVEN: with _STATE.md dirty, a bare 'git push origin main' invoked from P:/tmp passed exit 0. Documented as a deliberate tradeoff (:83-89, after it wrongly blocked a hauska-engine worktree push on 2026-08-09), so it is a known-cost design choice rather than an accident - but the gate protects nothing for any agent whose shell is parked outside doc_repo, which per the MEMORY note on persistent shell CWD is a common state.

hooks.purpose: Refuses git commit/push when doc_repo is not on branch main (single-branch workflow), and on detached HEAD.
hooks.evidence: Positive path only: on main, 'git commit -m test' passed exit 0 and benign 'ls -la' passed exit 0. The blocking branch could NOT be exercised without checking out a non-main branch in the live doc_repo working tree, which the constraints forbid (it would mutate operator state and risks the concurrent-commit hazard).
hooks.finding: UNTESTED for its blocking path - the only hook not proven to fire. Its guard is also weaker than it reads: it queries 'git -C P:/doc_repo branch --show-current' at :24 regardless of which repo the command targets, so a commit inside another repo or a worktree is judged against doc_repo's branch. That is fail-open for other repos (doc_repo on main means any foreign-repo commit passes) and fail-CLOSED-wrongly if doc_repo were ever off main. Low practical risk today (doc_repo is on main), but the control does not measure what its message claims.

hooks.purpose: M2 cadence. On Read of any *_STATE.md, regenerates _catalog/canon_divergence.md when the report is missing or older than 12 hours.
hooks.evidence: Report was 55.8 hours stale (mtime 2026-08-12 08:27, limit 12h). Fed a Read payload for P:/doc_repo/_STATE.md; hook ran the generator and report mtime advanced to 2026-08-14 16:17 with last_updated 2026-08-09 -> 2026-08-14 and refreshed commit counts (hauska-engine 10 -> 71, ldt 15 -> 44, mcp-server 0 -> 11). A Read payload for CLAUDE.md correctly no-opped.
hooks.finding: Fires correctly and is FAIL-OPEN BY DESIGN on every path (:4, :11 Exit-Open, always exit 0) - appropriate, since it is a detector not a gate. Two notes. (1) It is a control that SILENTLY MUTATES A TRACKED FILE as a side effect of a read, which means canon_divergence.md drifts dirty in the working tree without any agent intent; it was already showing ' M' at session start. (2) Its own staleness had reached 4.6x the 12h limit before this audit triggered it, meaning between 08-12 and 08-14 no agent Read a *_STATE.md path in a way that reached this hook, or the report would have refreshed. The detector's cadence depends on a read that may not happen.

files.summary: Tier-2 scratchpad capture (_scratch/<workstream>.md) with LESSON/DEAD-END/GROUND-TRUTH/OPEN entry kinds; planner-gated promotion to durable memory; prefers a mechanical guard over prose.
Read _STATE.md then MEMORY.md then the task doc before substantive work; restates the five standing decisions; update _STATE.md on handoff.

Sprint-scale work needs an operator-approved WDLL card before implementation; dispatches/PRs cite acceptance item numbers; re-grade item-by-item at close; thesis_parity_ledger entry when spine-model concepts are touched.
74 bytes; enables only the neon-postgres plugin. Carries no dev standard.

cursorConfig.trackedDetail: PARTIAL - 2 of 4 tracked. 'git ls-files .cursor/' returns only fleet-memory.mdc and read-state-first.mdc. wdll-practice.mdc and settings.json show '??' in git status.
cursorConfig.gitignoreStatus: NOT IGNORED. 'git check-ignore -v .cursor/settings.json .cursor/rules/wdll-practice.mdc .cursor/rules/fleet-memory.mdc .cursor/rules/read-state-first.mdc' exited 1 with zero output - no .gitignore rule matches any .cursor path, and .gitignore contains no .cursor entry at all.
cursorConfig.finding: The untracking is ACCIDENTAL, not deliberate - and that distinction is provable two ways: (1) no .gitignore rule matches, and (2) two SIBLING rules in the same directory ARE tracked, so the intent to version .cursor/rules is already established and wdll-practice.mdc simply never got added. wdll-practice.mdc is the higher-value loss: it is an alwaysApply dev standard governing sprint-scale work (WDLL card before implementation, acceptance-item citation, item-by-item re-grade at close) and it does not travel to another seat or survive a re-clone. That makes it protocol-shaped rather than structure-shaped, which is exactly the 0-for-3 class. Corroborating evidence that the practice IS live despite being untracked: _inbox/2026-08-14_l18_WDLL.md and _inbox/2026-08-14_l19_WDLL.md exist, and 90_runbooks/wdll_practice.md (the runbook the rule points to) is itself untracked ('??' in git status). So the entire WDLL control chain - rule plus runbook - is unversioned.
cursorConfig.recommendation: git add .cursor/rules/wdll-practice.mdc and 90_runbooks/wdll_practice.md, committing them alongside the two already-tracked rules; the whole .cursor/rules directory should be versioned as dev standards. .cursor/settings.json is a genuine judgment call - it holds only a local plugin toggle (neon-postgres) with no standard in it, so either commit it for seat parity or add an explicit '.cursor/settings.json' line to .gitignore so the exclusion is DECLARED rather than incidental. Leaving it merely-unadded is the worst of the three options because nothing records the intent.

Result: {"contractMarkerPresent":true,"contractDeclared":"4d5ddcd3","contractComputed":"4d5ddcd3","contractMatch":true,"preambleDeclared":"0f465c77","preambleComputed":"0f465c77","preambleMatch":true,"sdBodyLen":687}. Both the contract hash and the CANON-PREAMBLE hash (recomputed from the _STATE.md STANDING DECISIONS section per dispatch.mjs:68-75) match their declared markers. The compiler was NOT run in write mode; a read-only reimplementation was used because dispatch.mjs has no dry-run flag.
agentContract.compilerInUse: yes - _dispatches/ carries compiler-shaped output for l16 (08-13) and g0/l17/l18/l19/l20/l21/l22/l23/l24 (08-14). _dispatches/2026-08-14_g0_dispatch.md opens with 'CANON-PREAMBLE v0f465c77', 'AGENT-CONTRACT v4d5ddcd3', and 'PLAN-ROW: G-01, G-02, G-03, G-04, G-05 (90_operations/OPS-17_govtech_stack_plan_of_record.md)'.
agentContract.methodology: Parsed all 84 *_close.json artifacts in _inbox/ dated 2026-07-24..2026-08-14 and tested top-level key presence against the seven contract sections. Split at 2026-08-12, the date contract section 1 was ruled.

gaps.section: 1. Lane-planner fan model (two adversarial checkpoints, CP1 and CP2, each filed as a named _inbox/ artifact)
gaps.detail: Only 9 of 49 lanes (18%) filed a full CP1+CP2+close triad, and all 9 are the 08-14 L17-L22 cohort (l17, l18, l19, l20, l21, l21_followup3, l21_followup4, l21_followup5, l22). Every one of the 31 lanes closing on 08-12 filed a close with no CP1 and no CP2. 2026-08-12_W2_symnum_failclosed filed cp1 but no cp2. Two lanes (2026-08-13_l16, 2026-08-14_l24) filed both checkpoints but no close as of this audit. The requirement is measurably being adopted rather than met - the trend is sharply correct but the section as written is not yet describing behavior across the window.

gaps.direction: lanes non-compliant, improving sharply after the 08-12 ruling
gaps.detail: Top-level key presence, PRE (38 closes, 07-24..08-11) vs POST (46 closes, 08-12..08-14): lane id 13% -> 67%; PLAN-ROW 0% -> 65%; PR numbers 0% -> 28%; CI conclusion strings 50% -> 33%; checkpoint paths 61% -> 76%; counts 46% -> 48%; constraints-honored 0% -> 46%; open/remaining 13% -> 46%. PLAN-ROW went from literally never present to two-thirds, which is the ruling working. But PR numbers at 28% and CI conclusion strings at 33% are the weak fields, and CI conclusion presence actually DROPPED post-ruling. 2026-08-06_T1_elgin_close.json and 2026-08-09_E3_elgin_builder_close.json carry none of the eight fields.

gaps.section: 6. Close artifact - the contract names required fields in PROSE and never fixes a key schema
gaps.detail: Because section 6 lists fields as English prose, every lane invents its own keys and nothing can validate a close mechanically. Measured drift: key casing splits 38 camelCase / 6 snake_case / 2 mixed. PLAN-ROW appears as four different keys (planRow, plan_row, planRows, plan_rows). CI conclusion appears as five (ciConclusionString, ciConclusionStrings, ci_conclusion_strings, ldtCiConclusionString, pr293CiConclusionString). A contract that calls its close artifact 'machine-checkable' but pins no schema is protocol-shaped - the very shape the contract's own preamble says runs 0-for-3. There is no validator script in scripts/ that reads these files.

gaps.section: 7. Dispatch anatomy - 'a hand-assembled dispatch missing any marker is blocked by the canon-gate hook'
gaps.direction: contract too loose / claim not true as written
gaps.detail: The contract asserts the canon-gate hook blocks hand-assembled dispatches. For OPS-17 that assertion is FALSE: canon-gate's Test-PlanRows extracts only /P-\d+/, so every G-row dispatch - the entire govtech program this artifact belongs to - passes M5 unvalidated, as does any garbage string in the PLAN-ROW slot. Section 7 also says dispatches are 'generated by node scripts/dispatch.mjs' without naming the --plan flag, so a G-row dispatch compiled without '--plan OPS-17' fails the compiler's format check with an error the contract never explains.

gaps.section: 3. Write-slot law + lease ('slot custody is recorded in _STATE.md')
gaps.artifact: 42 of 76 close artifacts dated 2026-08-1x mention slot or lease
gaps.detail: Slot/lease discipline is visibly present in 55% of recent closes, which is the healthiest section-level adherence measured. Not raised as a defect; recorded so the contrast with sections 1 and 6 is visible - the sections lanes follow best are the ones with a concrete named mechanism (the lease FAILS CLOSED), and the sections they follow worst are the ones expressed as prose obligations.

deadControlsNote: NONE. All five hook files in .claude/hooks/ are referenced by .claude/settings.json: branch-guard.ps1 and dirty-tree-close-gate.ps1 on the Bash matcher, canon-gate.ps1 and dispatch-template-gate.ps1 on the Agent|Write matcher, canon-divergence-run.ps1 on the Read matcher. No orphan hook file, and no settings.json entry pointing at a nonexistent file. settings.local.json contains only a permission allow-rule and declares no hooks. The dead-control risk in this repo is NOT an unreferenced file - it is a wired hook whose predicate silently never matches, which is exactly what ranked findings 1 and 2 are.

rankedFindings.title: canon-gate M5 PLAN-ROW validation is entirely inert for OPS-17 (G-rows) and for any malformed row id
rankedFindings.evidence: canon-gate.ps1:258 matches only /P-\d+/; :259 returns 'ok' when the set is empty. PROVEN by negative test: PLAN-ROW G-9999 exit 0, Q-42 exit 0, 'not-a-row-at-all' exit 0, while P-9999 correctly exits 2.
rankedFindings.impact: The entire govtech program (OPS-17, 37 rows) dispatches with zero PLAN-ROW enforcement, including this dispatch's own G-05. 'No row, no dispatch' is not being enforced for half the active programs. The gate LOOKS live because P-row tests pass.
rankedFindings.recommendedFix: Make the row-id regex and the plan file selection data-driven from the same PLANS map dispatch.mjs uses (P->OPS-16, G->OPS-17), and change the empty-rowIds fallthrough at :259 from fail-open to a block, since a PLAN-ROW line whose value matches no known program is by definition unscoped.

rankedFindings.title: canon-gate M1 no-touch gate misses the most natural way to name a repo
rankedFindings.evidence: Resolve-RepoFromText (canon-gate.ps1:85-98) has no pattern for a bare unquoted 'P:/<repo>'. PROVEN: 'Work in P:/smartcity-os and open a PR' exit 0; the same brief with 'repo: smartcity-os', 'Working in P:/smartcity-os', quoted `P:/smartcity-os/`, 'git -C P:/smartcity-os', or the gh org slug all exit 2.
rankedFindings.impact: smartcity-os is ABSOLUTE NO-TOUCH (repo_intents.md:69, live prod for Bastrop). A hand-written brief that names it in the ordinary way sails through the gate. The intents parser itself is correct - it resolves smartcity-os=no-touch and the doc is 6 days old against a 30-day limit - so the failure is purely in resolution.
rankedFindings.recommendedFix: Add an unanchored alternation for bare 'P:[/\\]<known-repo>' to Resolve-RepoFromText, and consider resolving on the repo NAME alone anywhere in the text for no-touch repos specifically, accepting false positives on a short no-touch list since CANON_OVERRIDE already exists as the escape hatch.

rankedFindings.title: Contract section 6 calls the close artifact 'machine-checkable' but pins no schema, and nothing checks it
rankedFindings.evidence: Four PLAN-ROW key spellings, five CI-conclusion key spellings, 38/6/2 camel/snake/mixed casing across 46 recent closes. No validator exists in scripts/.
rankedFindings.impact: The close artifact is the program's primary evidence surface. As written it is machine-READABLE but not machine-CHECKED, so a lane can file a close missing PRs, CI strings, and counts and nothing detects it - measured at 28% and 33% presence for PRs and CI strings post-ruling.
rankedFindings.recommendedFix: Pin a JSON schema in the contract (fixed key names, one casing) and add scripts/validate-close.mjs that exits non-zero on a missing required key. This converts section 6 from protocol-shaped to hook-shaped, which is the whole thesis of the base-rate argument in dispatch-template-gate.ps1:11-16.

rankedFindings.title: Section 1's two-adversarial-checkpoint requirement is met by 18% of lanes
rankedFindings.evidence: 9 of 49 lanes closing 08-12..08-14 filed full CP1+CP2+close triads; all 9 are the 08-14 L17-L22 cohort. All 31 lanes closing 08-12 filed a close with neither checkpoint.
rankedFindings.impact: The in-process adversarial check is the contract's main defense against a narrated close. Direction of travel is strongly correct (0% on 08-12 to near-universal on 08-14), so this is an adoption curve rather than a dead rule - but the contract currently describes an aspiration for most of the measured window.
rankedFindings.recommendedFix: Nothing structural if the 08-14 rate holds; re-measure at the next program close. If it slips, the enforceable version is the same validator as finding 3 refusing a close whose named cp1/cp2 paths do not exist on disk.

rankedFindings.title: The entire WDLL control chain is unversioned
rankedFindings.evidence: .cursor/rules/wdll-practice.mdc and 90_runbooks/wdll_practice.md both show '??'. git check-ignore exits 1 with no output - no .gitignore rule matches. Two sibling rules in the same directory ARE tracked.
rankedFindings.impact: An alwaysApply dev standard governing all sprint-scale work does not travel to another seat and does not survive a re-clone, and neither does the runbook it points at. Protocol-shaped by construction.
rankedFindings.recommendedFix: Commit both files. Separately decide .cursor/settings.json explicitly - commit it or add a named .gitignore line - so the exclusion is declared rather than incidental.

rankedFindings.title: dirty-tree-close-gate protects nothing when the shell cwd is outside doc_repo
rankedFindings.evidence: With _STATE.md worktree-dirty, a bare 'git push origin main' from P:/tmp passed exit 0 (dirty-tree-close-gate.ps1:94-99).
rankedFindings.impact: The stale-state failure this gate exists to prevent is fully reachable from any non-doc_repo shell. Given the recorded shell-CWD-persists hazard, that is a routine state, not an edge case.
rankedFindings.recommendedFix: Documented tradeoff (:83-89) so do not simply revert it. Better predicate: resolve the push's actual target with 'git rev-parse --show-toplevel' from the command's own directory rather than inferring from cwd string-matching.

rankedFindings.title: dispatch-template-gate checks clauses by bare substring, so prose ABOUT a clause satisfies the clause
rankedFindings.evidence: Measured during testing: a brief stating 'no exit-bounded verification language, and no named close artifact path' satisfied checks 3 and 4, collapsing a four-clause failure to one. The :153 alternation also accepts the bare word 'timeout'.
rankedFindings.impact: A brief can pass the gate while carrying no actual rule. The gate's block is real (proven) but its pass is weak.
rankedFindings.recommendedFix: Require the clauses in structural positions the way check 2 already does for no-nesting (first non-empty line) - e.g. an explicit '_inbox/<path>.json' capture for check 4 rather than the loose phrase 'close artifact', and drop 'timeout' from the check-3 alternation.

rankedFindings.title: branch-guard's blocking path is unproven and it measures the wrong repo
rankedFindings.evidence: Only the pass path was exercised (on main: commit exit 0, ls exit 0). Blocking would require checking out a non-main branch in the live tree, which constraints forbid. Source :24 queries 'git -C P:/doc_repo branch --show-current' regardless of the command's target repo.
rankedFindings.impact: The one hook not proven to fire. Its guard is also scoped to doc_repo's branch while matching every Bash command, so foreign-repo commits are judged against doc_repo's state.
rankedFindings.recommendedFix: Resolve the branch from the command's actual working directory, and exercise the block path once in a throwaway clone rather than the live tree.

rankedFindings.title: canon-divergence report had drifted to 4.6x its own staleness limit, and refreshing it silently dirties a tracked file
rankedFindings.evidence: Report mtime 2026-08-12 08:27, i.e. 55.8h against a 12h limit, until this audit's Read payload triggered the refresh to 2026-08-14 16:17. The refresh rewrote a tracked file (_catalog/canon_divergence.md, last committed 2026-08-09) as a side effect of a read.
rankedFindings.impact: The cadence depends on an agent reading a *_STATE.md path through this hook; between 08-12 and 08-14 that did not happen. Refreshed counts were materially different (hauska-engine 10 -> 71 commits), so the report was stale in substance, not just in date. Separately, a read mutating tracked state is a surprising side effect that leaves the tree dirty with no agent intent.
rankedFindings.recommendedFix: Keep it fail-open, but make staleness visible where it is read - surface the report's age in _STATE.md GOVERNANCE, or write the refreshed report to an ignored path and only promote deliberately.

openQuestions: Should canon-gate's M5 read the PLANS map from a shared source with scripts/dispatch.mjs so a new program (a future OPS-18) is gated the day it is created rather than silently exempt? Today the compiler knows both plans and the hook knows only one.
Is the 46-close key drift worth a one-time normalization pass, or only a schema pin going forward? A validator that rejects the existing corpus is a validator nobody will run.

Was the operator's intent for .cursor/settings.json to be per-seat local (in which case it belongs in .gitignore explicitly) or shared? The file holds only a neon-postgres plugin toggle, which reads local, but nothing records the decision.

branch-guard has never been proven to block. Is it worth exercising in a throwaway clone, or is the single-branch workflow now enforced well enough by convention that the hook should be retired rather than repaired? The repo has precedent for deleting an unfired rung (the session-close grading rung, 0 of 215).

CI-conclusion-string presence DROPPED from 50% to 33% after the 08-12 ruling, against every other field rising. Is that a real regression, a shift in what lanes were doing (more DB/data lanes with no PRs), or an artifact of key-name drift? Worth one reconciliation pass - two numbers that should agree and don't.
